Numerical investigation of heat transfer and flow stability in a shear driven Carreau fluid

Abstract:

This study presents a mathematical and numerical investigation of the flow and thermal trans port characteristics of a Carreau fluid over a permeable stretching/shrinking sheet subjected to uniform shear. The governing nonlinear partial differential equations are reduced to a coupled system of ordinary differential equations using Lie group analysis and similarity transforma tions and solved numerically using the bvp4c solver in MATLAB. The effects of fluid rheology, surface transpiration, and thermal radiation on the momentum and thermal boundary layers are examined. The results reveal dual solution branches over a finite range of the stretch ing/shrinking parameter, originating from a critical bifurcation point. Linear stability analysis confirms that the upper solution branch is stable and represents the physically realizable flow state. The findings demonstrate that fluid rheology and surface transpiration significantly in fluence flow and heat transfer, providing useful insights into thermal management processes involving shear-dependent non-Newtonian fluids.
